title: Sleep: the student's forgotten friend
text:
Ask any student about exam season and you are likely to hear stories of revision sessions that stretched into the {1} hours. Many will proudly admit to having pulled an all-{2} before a deadline, as if staying awake were a badge of honour.

{3} the midnight oil may feel productive at the time, but the evidence suggests otherwise. Memory depends heavily on sleep, and students who are constantly sleep-{4} tend to remember less of what they have studied, not more. Over time, a lack of rest also {5} its toll on mood, concentration and even physical health.

Many students assume they can simply catch {6} on sleep at the weekend. Unfortunately, the body does not work quite like a bank account, and a long lie-in on Sunday cannot fully make up for a week of late nights.

So what should students do? First and {7}, they should treat sleep as part of their study plan rather than an obstacle to it. When in doubt, it is wiser to {8} on the side of caution and go to bed than to revise for one more hour with a tired brain.

items.hint: Which adjective completes the expression for the hours just after midnight?
items.explanation: 'The small hours' are the hours after midnight (1, 2, 3 a.m.). The expression is fixed.

items.hint: Complete the informal expression for staying up all night to work.
items.explanation: 'To pull an all-nighter' means to stay awake all night, usually to study or work.

items.hint: Complete the idiom meaning 'to work late into the night'.
items.explanation: 'To burn the midnight oil' means to work until very late at night. The idiom always uses 'burn'.

items.hint: Which adjective forms a compound with 'sleep-' meaning 'not getting enough sleep'?
items.explanation: 'Sleep-deprived' means not getting enough sleep. 'Deficient' is used with 'in' (deficient in vitamins), and 'drained' means exhausted in general.

items.hint: Complete the expression '… its toll on something', meaning 'damage it gradually'.
items.explanation: 'To take its toll on' something means to have a gradual harmful effect on it.

items.hint: Which particle makes 'catch … on sleep' mean 'get the sleep you missed'?
items.explanation: 'To catch up on' sleep (or work) means to do what you should have done earlier.

items.hint: Complete the fixed phrase 'first and …', meaning 'most importantly'.
items.explanation: 'First and foremost' means 'above all, most importantly'. The phrase is fixed.

items.hint: Complete the idiom meaning 'to be extra careful when you are not sure'.
items.explanation: 'To err on the side of caution' means to choose the safer option. The idiom always uses 'err'.

title: The true cost of a cheap T-shirt
text:
Fast fashion has made clothes more {1} than ever before. A T-shirt can now cost less than a sandwich, and many shoppers buy new outfits for a single party, wear them once and throw them away. For many young people, clothes have effectively become disposable. What is less visible are the environmental {2} of this habit.

Producing a single pair of jeans requires an almost {3} amount of water, and much of the clothing we buy ends up in landfill sites {4} quickly. The human cost can be just as high. Garment workers are often paid {5} low wages, and conditions in some factories remain genuinely {6}.

Growing {7} of these problems has led a number of brands to promise change, from using recycled materials to paying fairer wages. Many critics, however, remain {8}. They point out that as long as the industry depends on selling ever larger quantities of cheap clothes, small improvements will do little to change the overall picture.

items.hint: An adjective after 'more': clothes that people can pay for easily.
items.explanation: 'Affordable' means cheap enough for people to buy: afford + -able.

items.hint: A plural noun after 'the environmental' (look at the verb 'are').
items.explanation: 'Consequences' are results, usually negative ones. The verb 'are' tells you the noun must be plural.

items.hint: An adjective after 'an almost', describing a huge amount.
items.explanation: 'An almost unbelievable amount' is so large that it is hard to believe: un- + believe + -able.
'Surprisingly quickly' means more quickly than you would expect. You need an adverb to modify another adverb.

items.hint: An adverb before 'low' with a negative meaning.
items.explanation: 'Unacceptably low wages' are so low that they should not be allowed: un- + accept + -able + -ly.
'Dangerous' is the adjective from 'danger': conditions that can cause harm.

items.hint: After 'Growing' you need a noun followed by 'of'.
items.explanation: 'Growing awareness of' a problem means more and more people know about it: aware + -ness.

items.hint: An adjective after 'remain': the critics still don't believe it.
items.explanation: 'Remain unconvinced' means they still don't believe the promises: un- + convince + -d.
